01 / A CONSISTENT CALENDAR

First Monday. Then Tuesday.

For every year, we calculate the Tuesday after the first Monday in November (November 2–8). Federal election years are even-numbered; presidential years are divisible by four. “All years” applies the same calendar rule to off-years without claiming a federal election took place.

The date labels identify the calendar comparison. Our source is a November monthly DFW price average, not an observed daily election-day quote. Monthly averages may include observations after election day and are retrospective, not information necessarily available that Tuesday.

Election calendar · National Archives ↗

03 / THE MATH

One price. Three useful perspectives.

Inflation-adjusted priceprice × (reference-year CPI ÷ year CPI)

Expresses the price in reference-year purchasing power. Choose the DFW or U.S. all-items CPI.

Wage-adjusted priceprice × (reference-year wage ÷ year wage)

The dollar price with an equivalent share of reference-year gross hourly earnings.

Time & buying powerminutes / gallon = 60 × price ÷ hourly wage
gallons / work-hour = hourly wage ÷ price

A fill-up costs 14.5 × the per-gallon price and takes 14.5 × the per-gallon minutes. An hour’s pay buys wage ÷ (14.5 × price) fill-ups. Work metrics use nominal wages and prices from the same year; applying the same inflation factor to both cancels out.

04 / KNOW WHAT YOU’RE LOOKING AT

History and estimates stay distinct.

Historical proxy means the November monthly input has been published. These are source observations, not daily election-day measurements; historical wage series may be revised by BLS.

Preliminary estimate means one or more November 2026 inputs were unavailable at the snapshot. Each unavailable input is held flat at its latest published month. This is a transparent carry-forward scenario, not an official BLS November reading or a statistical forecast. Dashed lines, outlined points, and amber labels preserve that distinction throughout the site.

No missing historical November price, CPI, or wage is backfilled. DFW published CPI in even-numbered months before 1998, so November DFW inflation adjustments are unavailable for 1978–1997. Choose the U.S. CPI option for those earlier years. No wage before 2007 is invented. The 2026 reference year is excluded because its November inputs are incomplete. You can exclude preliminary records from the explorer with one switch.

Average hourly earnings describe the average private-sector job, not median household income or take-home pay. This does not account for taxes, driving distance, fuel efficiency, or differences between individual workers and stations. Changes in costs alone do not establish political causation.

The site is a fixed snapshot; it does not update automatically. Exported data includes input months, status, adjustment, and reference year.
